mechanism: Sort-free parity row generation for cold (layout-miss) GF(2) Macaulay builds in build_macaulay_packed (src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_groebner.rs). Each monomial of degree <= D (D <= 6) in n <= 64 variables gets a direct colex slot (at most 2^20 slots). For each product t*f the code toggles slots in a thread-local parity bitset, so even multiplicities cancel. It reads the odd slots back in term order and marks first-seen columns in a seen bitset. It then sorts only the distinct columns (same mono_key order) and scatters the rows through a slot->column table. This removes the per-row sort, the per-row Vec allocation, the hash-set column discovery and the hashed column lookups during packing. Rows, row order, columns, caps, layout-cache side effects and the bitop/v1 tally (charged with the old formulas) stay the same. Fallback to the old builder for degree > 6, more than 2^20 slots, support outside n_vars, or when a cached layout is present. Baseline profile: row generation was 53% of macaulay_profile Ir on the Koblitz n=31 cell. The M4RI/RREF elimination is unchanged.
prediction: Written before measuring: rows/cols/rank, rref word_ops, bitop tally, stage verdicts and word_ops, crossbred verdicts and bit ops, and f4_fp fingerprints all identical. Callgrind x build 38.0M -> about 8-12M Ir and macaulay_profile 71M -> about 42-45M Ir (about 1.6x). Production stage gain small single-digit % or less, because layout hits dominate. Outcome: the identity predictions held. The size prediction missed: build 21.2M Ir and profile 1.31x. The production-stage prediction held (-0.2% to -0.5%).

risks: The gain is confined to cold (layout-miss) Macaulay builds: the kernel bench, MatrixF4 nodes and InheritedF4 roots on misses. Total Ir in the production stage ladder moves by less than 1%. The thread-local scratch grows to the largest slot space seen (up to 2^20 slots: two 128 KiB bitsets plus a 4 MiB slot_col) and never shrinks. A panic mid-build has no unwind guard and could leave the parity/seen bits dirty for later builds on that thread. The layout-cache side effects (miss counter, insertion, eviction) are mirrored by hand, so a future change there must be mirrored too. Merge conflicts are likely at the single dispatch point in build_macaulay_packed and at its new ParityPack bound if other leads change that function. The cost prediction missed (1.31x instead of the predicted 1.6x on the profile). All 3 builds are used. Tests were run from the test binary my build 3 produced, copied to bin/crypto_lib_test, because the two-word TEST_FILTER made cargo run 0 tests.
